howDoI.q: How do I show the same place by day and by night?
How do I make a window or a lamp that only lights at night?
How do I hide a star until it is night?
How do I change the palette when the player walks somewhere?
How do I make a sunset in steps?
How do I fade from one look to another?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Day and Night is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels, about a minute each, and a map that is shown in more than one set of colors.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score.

Nothing in this game hurts you. Coins add to your score.

pages.head: Level 1: One Map, Two Looks
pages.html:
Level 1: One Map, Two Looks

Three signs stand in a sunny yard in front of a house. One says the room has two palettes, one says the sun and the moon are one block, and one says the door goes to a new scene with a new palette. Four coins lie on the porch, and the door is at its end.

Go in the door. You come out at the start of the very same yard, but now it is night: the sky is dark, the sun has become a moon, the windows and the lantern are lit and stars are out. It is the same map file and the same block file, with a different palette. The door in the night yard goes on to level 2.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A palette is a file. A block is a 20 by 20 picture, and each of its pixels is a number from 0 to 254, the slot of a color. It is the palette file that says what each slot looks like. day.pal and night.pal are each 256 colors, and they list the same slots in the same order.
  • Two scenes, one map. Open dayngt.gam in the Scenes editor. Scene 2 and scene 3 name the same map (one.map) and the same blocks (one.bbl). They differ in one slot: scene 2 has day.pal as its palette and scene 3 has night.pal.
  • One block, two looks. The orb block is a disc drawn from three slots. In day.pal those slots are gold, so it is a sun. In night.pal they are silver, and it is a moon. Nothing in the map changes.
  • Lights. The window and lantern blocks use three slots of dull glass in day.pal and three of warm light in night.pal. That is all it takes for the house to light up.
  • Stars. The star block is drawn in one slot, and in day.pal that slot is exactly the sky's color. The stars are in the sky all day; you cannot see them. In night.pal the slot is pale yellow.
  • Kit. Kit is drawn from slots too (hero.cbl shares the palette), so he would turn dark with everything else. The night palette keeps his colors bright so he is easy to follow.
  • The door. A link in scene 2 on the door's bottom block goes to scene 3, with the hero landing at the start. The same cell in scene 3 has a link to level 2. A link belongs to a scene, not to the map, so the same door can go two places.
  • The fade. Every scene fades its map in from black when it starts, and fades to black when you leave it, so the change from day to night is a fade out, then a fade in.

pages.head: Level 2: Sundown Street
pages.html:
Level 2: Sundown Street

A street with two stone gates and a cottage at the end. The sky is blue, the sun is out and three signs stand along the way. Walk through the first gate. The sky goes orange: it is dusk. Walk through the second gate: night, with a moon, stars and lit street lamps. The last sign and the cottage's door are in the dark.

The sunset is not one thing that moves. It is three scenes, each with its own palette, and a gate that takes you from one to the next. Walk back through the first gate when you are at dusk, if you like: nothing happens, because gates only go one way. There are four coins in the first two parts.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Three palettes. day.pal and night.pal are the ones from level 1. dusk.pal is the third: the same slots with a warm sky and an orange sun.
  • Three scenes, one map. In dayngt.gam, scenes 4, 5 and 6 all name two.map and two.bbl. They differ in their palette (day.pal, dusk.pal, night.pal) and in the links.
  • The gates. Scene 4 has a link on the cells in the middle of the first gate. It goes to scene 5, and the hero lands on the street just beyond the gate, so it feels like walking on. Scene 5 has a link in the second gate that goes to scene 6, and scene 6 has one on the cottage door that goes to the ending. There is no link in scene 5 on the first gate, which is why walking back does nothing.
  • The gate is only a picture. The pillars and lintel have nothing in their Solid boxes. They show you where to walk; the link is what does the work.
  • No level card after the first. Only scene 4 has a level card. Scenes 5 and 6 have no card in their file list, so the next thing you see after the gate is the street fading in.
  • The street lamps. The lamp blocks use the same three "lamp" slots as the windows, so they glow at night with no extra work.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A palette is one file for the whole scene. Some things you may expect are not there:

  • It cannot show more than 256 colors at once. Slot 255 is kept as "clear", so there are 255 to share between the sky, the ground, the signs, Kit and everything else. A palette for night has to fit the same 255 slots that the day palette uses.
  • Both palettes share the same block art. A block is a picture of slot numbers, so a block cannot look different from one palette to the next in anything but color. If you want a different shape at night, such as a lit window with curtains, it has to be a different block, with its own place in the map.
  • It cannot change the palette in the middle of a scene. A scene loads one palette when it starts. A time of day that changes while the hero stands still needs a link to another scene, so the change is made by taking the hero there. Here, the gates are links.
  • It cannot cross-fade from one palette to another. Every scene fades its map in from black, and fades out to black when it ends. A smooth blend from day to night needs a cartoon (an FLI file), which can change the palette frame by frame.
  • A link goes one way. To walk back to the day you would give the dusk scene a link back to the day scene.
  • A palette change shows on everything in the scene at once: the sky, the ground and the hero. You cannot light one corner and darken another with the palette alone; that takes different blocks.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Open night.pal in the Palette editor and change the sky's slot to a deep purple. Level 1 and level 2 both change.
  • Change the three "orb" slots in dusk.pal to red, and the sun sets red.
  • In the Scenes editor, change scene 3's palette from night.pal to dusk.pal. Level 1 now goes from day to dusk.
  • Copy scene 5, call it "dawn", give it dusk.pal and a link back to the day scene in the first gate, and the sunset will have a sunrise too.
  • Draw a new block for a curtain in the Blocks tab and put it in front of a window in the map. It is the same at any hour, so a lit window needs its own slot.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
